output.brief: Pellacott's 2026-built VA-220 valves are the problem. They are not an installer or firmware problem. A Brenmoor lab teardown found the internal seal deformed and unseated in 38 of 41 returned valves. Helium retests of unused warehouse stock found 11% of Pellacott's 2026 valves leaking, against about 1% for 2025 builds and 0% for Durrant-Hale. Matched claim rates are the same across new and legacy installers and across firmware 4.1 and 4.2. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's VA-220 leak rig out of service since January 2026. No other rig has a VA-220 test program. The 2026 certificates repeat four fixed sequences of values, some already used in 2025 certificates. So the certificates do not record real tests. The SupplierPath score rose because complete, in-limit records earned credit, not because quality improved. Next steps: quarantine all 2026 Pellacott stock, including the six held lots, and do not release them on fresh certificates. Suspend dock-to-stock, and run Brenmoor's own helium testing before any release. Drop the installer remediation plan. Dual-source more from Durrant-Hale to cover the line stoppage. Require rig logs or witnessed tests for test-record credit. Check other suppliers' records. The seal change and the Line 3 move cannot yet be told apart, so ask Pellacott for details of both before directing a seal switch.
